trial.title: XCures/Cancer Commons Enhanced Learning Treatment Selection and Analysis with Outcomes Research (XCELSIOR) Study: A Patient-Centric Platform Trial for Precision Oncology

inclusion.description: Patient or legally authorized representative able to understand and willing to provide electronically signed and dated Informed Consent. Patient able to provide assent, if applicable.
Patient or legally-authorized representative willing and able to provide electronically signed and dated Patient Advocacy Agreement.
Medical history or diagnosis of cancer (any type, including recalcitrant, advanced, or metastatic cancer).

exclusion.description: Patient is not a resident of or receiving care within the United States or US territories.
exclusion.note: Patients MUST be resident of or receiving care within the US or US territories. Non-US patients are excluded.

notes: No restrictions on performance status, comorbidities, or disease severity.
Pediatric patients are eligible (with legally authorized representative consent).
No restrictions on cancer type — any cancer diagnosis qualifies.
This is a non-interventional registry; no treatment is assigned.
Patients with only suspected cancer (not yet confirmed) may also be eligible.

test_patients.scenario: Clearly Eligible — Adult US patient with confirmed cancer

diagnoses: Stage IV Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

expected_assessments.reasoning: Patient is an adult able to provide informed consent. No cognitive or legal barriers noted.
Patient is able to sign agreements; no barriers noted.
Confirmed Stage IV NSCLC diagnosis clearly satisfies the cancer diagnosis criterion.
Patient is a US resident (Chicago, IL). The exclusion criterion does NOT apply — patient is eligible.
Patient is competent and able to provide informed consent.
Patient is able to sign the Patient Advocacy Agreement.
Confirmed GBM diagnosis satisfies the cancer diagnosis criterion.
Patient resides in Canada and is not receiving care in the US or US territories. This exclusion criterion applies — patient is INELIGIBLE.

test_patients.scenario: Needs Review — Suspected cancer, not yet confirmed

expected_assessments.reasoning: Patient is an adult and able to provide informed consent.
Patient is able to sign the Patient Advocacy Agreement.

Patient has suspected but not yet confirmed cancer (biopsy pending). The protocol states 'known or suspected' cancer is eligible, but the AI should flag this for clinician review to confirm interpretation.
expected_assessments.follow_up: Confirm whether 'suspected cancer' alone meets I3, or whether biopsy confirmation is required before enrollment.

expected_assessments.reasoning: Patient is a US resident (Houston, TX). Not excluded on geographic grounds.

test_patients.scenario: Eligible — Pediatric patient with legally authorized representative

expected_assessments.reasoning: Patient is a minor (age 9), but a legally authorized representative (parent/guardian) is present and able to provide informed consent on behalf of the patient. Protocol explicitly allows for LAR consent and patient assent.
LAR is willing and able to sign the Patient Advocacy Agreement on behalf of the patient.
Confirmed DIPG diagnosis. Protocol includes pediatric cancers as a specific substudy area.
Patient is a US resident (Boston, MA). Not excluded.

evaluation_rubric.description: How to score TrailMatch AI output against this ground truth

criteria_extraction_score.full_credit: All 3 inclusion criteria and 1 exclusion criterion identified with accurate descriptions
criteria_extraction_score.no_credit: Fewer than 2 criteria or major description errors

per_patient_scoring.per_criterion: 1 point per criterion assessment matching expected_status

edge_cases_to_watch: TP-003: Does the model correctly flag suspected (unconfirmed) cancer as INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than hard-failing?
TP-004: Does the model recognize that a pediatric patient can be eligible via LAR consent?
E1: Does the model correctly treat geographic location as an exclusion (not inclusion) criterion?
